mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces discount rates applied to expected corporate cash flows, lowering the present value of future earnings and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite persistent FEDFUNDS > 4% for 6 months, or discount rate sensitivity (MRW) estimates are negative and statistically insignificant.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: No significant correlation between PAYEMS growth and UNRATE declines over 60 days, or SPX 60-day returns are negative despite meeting trigger condition (p > 0.05 in OLS regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,200 suggests cooling demand for housing, which reduces construction sector earnings and dampens overall economic momentum, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST recovers above 1200 within 2 months, or 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in consumer goods orders (not available in proxy list - so skip interaction) -- instead, use GDPC1 as proxy for demand shock that reduces supply response, leading to negative 20-day forward returns when triggered by a sudden drop in GDPC1.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 drops by > 5% in a single month
failure_condition: GDPC1 recovers without a corresponding S&P 500 decline in the 20-day window, or 20-day returns are positive despite the drop (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2% for two consecutive months during a period of rising FEDFUNDS, the market anticipates tighter policy, causing a sharp decline in equity valuations and negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 2% and FEDFUNDS increases over the same month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive despite CPIAUCSL > 2% and rising FEDFUNDS (p < 0.05 in regression).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% without a corresponding rise in labor participation suggests a mature labor market, which reduces growth prospects and yields negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE rises above 4% with SPX 60-day returns positive (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-time monthly drop in retail sales proxy (not available - so use PAYEMS as proxy for consumer demand) followed by a sustained rise in consumer confidence index (not available - so use a combination of HOUST and PAYEMS) indicates weakening demand, producing negative 20-day returns when the drop persists.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by > 3% while PAYEMS remains flat for two months
failure_condition: Both proxies revert to growth or SPX 20-day returns are positive despite the trigger (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a supply chain disruption (indicated by a sharp one-time drop in GDPC1 followed by elevated industrial production volatility (not available - so use INDPRO volatility via change)), the market anticipates production bottlenecks, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as firms raise prices and boost profits.
failure_condition: No significant SPX 60-day return increase despite the GDPC1 shock (p > 0.05 in event study).
